subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw add Markdown code-fence linting to workspace writes, and should the default be auto-fix, warn-only, explicit opt-in, or no core mutation?
rationale: The request changes persisted workspace content and adds config/API surface, while prior implementation attempts exposed parser edge cases that could corrupt real Markdown.

options.title: Warn-First Or Opt-In Lint
options.body: Add parser-backed diagnostics or an explicit opt-in fix mode first so existing workspace writes remain byte-preserving by default.

options.title: Default Auto-Fix
options.body: Rewrite workspace Markdown automatically at write time, accepting higher compatibility and content-mutation risk for stronger formatting guarantees.

options.title: No Core Write-Time Mutation
options.body: Keep core writes raw and rely on prompts, docs linting, or external tooling unless a narrower runtime bug requires a core hook.

recommendation.title: Warn-First Or Opt-In Lint
recommendation.body: Add parser-backed diagnostics or an explicit opt-in fix mode first so existing workspace writes remain byte-preserving by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main ownership evidence points to this account on the workspace write and Markdown helper paths that would need the policy decision implemented.
